hints: Focus on how bonding changes across Period 3, from ionic on the left to molecular covalent on the right.
Remember that $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is amphoteric and giant, while $\text{SiO}_2$ is a giant covalent solid with a very high melting point.
Connect giant structures to high melting points and simple molecular structures to low melting points to pick the fully correct row.
walkthrough:
**Recall the Period 3 oxide trend**

Think left to right: metallic to non-metallic character increases. So oxides change from basic to amphoteric to acidic.

Key identities: $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is amphoteric, $\text{SiO}_2$ and $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$ are acidic.

**Link structure to melting point**

Giant structures need lots of energy to break, so they melt high. Simple molecules have only weak intermolecular forces, so they melt low.

$$\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3 \text{ (giant ionic lattice) , } \text{SiO}_2 \text{ (giant covalent lattice) } \rightarrow \text{high melting point}$$
$$\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10} \text{ (simple molecular) } \rightarrow \text{low melting point}$$

**Check reaction with water**

Only the non-metal oxides that dissolve easily react vigorously. $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$ reacts vigorously to give acid, but $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ and $\text{SiO}_2$ are insoluble and do not react.

$$\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10} + 6\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 4\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$$

**Pick the fully correct row**

The only row that gets all three oxides right for melting point is high, high, low. That matches structure perfectly, so it is the correct choice.

options.A: Incorrect because the acid-base labels are shifted. $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is amphoteric (reacts with both acids and alkalis), not basic. $\text{SiO}_2$ is weakly acidic, not amphoteric. Only $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$ is correctly called acidic.
options.B: Incorrect because $\text{SiO}_2$ is not giant ionic. It is a giant covalent (macromolecular) lattice of Si-O bonds. $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is essentially giant ionic and $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$ is simple molecular, but the middle column spoils this row.
options.C: Correct because structure controls melting point. $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ (giant ionic) and $\text{SiO}_2$ (giant covalent) both need strong bonds broken throughout the lattice, so high melting point. $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$ is simple molecular with weak van der Waals forces between molecules, so low melting point.
options.D: Incorrect because $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ and $\text{SiO}_2$ are insoluble and show no reaction with water. Only $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$ reacts vigorously with water to form phosphoric acid. Students often assume all oxides react, but giant oxides are too stable and insoluble to do so.
